title: Interior and Boundary Sobolev Elliptic Regularity

items.title: Difference quotients on a shrunken domain
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev interfaces used below. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$, let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
([[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]]). For
$h\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $e_i$ be the
$i$-th standard unit vector and put
$$\Omega_{i,h}:=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}=\Omega\cap(\Omega-he_i),$$
an open subset of $\Omega$, since it is the intersection of the open set
$\Omega$ with the preimage of $\Omega$ under the homeomorphism
$x\mapsto x+he_i$. The **$i$-th difference quotient of $u$ of size $h$** is
$$\delta_h^iu(x):=\frac{u(x+he_i)-u(x)}{h},\qquad x\in\Omega_{i,h},$$
read on the almost-everywhere classes
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); the
**difference-quotient vector** is
$$\delta_hu:=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu),$$
defined on the open intersection $\Omega_h:=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_{i,h}$,
while each component is defined on its own shrunken set $\Omega_{i,h}$.

Throughout this page the translation notation is the published one of
[[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]], namely
$\tau_hu(x)=u(x-h)$; consequently the forward shift that occurs in the
product rule is the translate by $-he_i$:
$$u(x+he_i)=(\tau_{-he_i}u)(x),\qquad \delta_h^iu=\frac{\tau_{-he_i}u-u}{h}\quad\text{on }\Omega_{i,h}.$$

For the open upper half-space
$H=\{x_n>0\}$ and a **tangential**
index $j<n$, the translation $x\mapsto x+he_j$ maps $H$ onto $H$; hence
$\delta_h^ju$ is defined on all of $H$. For the **normal** index $n$ and
$h>0$ one has $H_{n,h}=H$ (since $x_n>0$ implies $x_n+h>0$), while for
$h<0$ one has $H_{n,h}=\{x\in H:x_n>|h|\}$, a proper subset of $H$.

**Well-definedness.** Both values $u(x)$ and $u(x+he_i)$ in the numerator are
defined for every $x\in\Omega_{i,h}$, and
$$|\delta_h^iu(x)|\le\frac{|u(x+he_i)|+|u(x)|}{|h|},$$
so $\delta_h^iu\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega_{i,h};\mathbb K)$: on a compact
$K\Subset\Omega_{i,h}$ the first term is controlled by
$\int_K|u(x+he_i)|\,dx=\int_{K+he_i}|u(y)|\,dy<\infty$, because
$K+he_i$ is a compact subset of $\Omega$, and the second term is controlled
on $K\Subset\Omega$. Further, the definition depends only on the class of
$u$: if $u=\widetilde u$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $E\subseteq\Omega$
is a null set with $u=\widetilde u$ on $\Omega\setminus E$, then
$\delta_h^iu\ne\delta_h^i\widetilde u$ only at points of
$(\Omega_{i,h}\cap E)\cup(\Omega_{i,h}\cap(E-he_i))$, a null set because
$E$ is null and $E-he_i$ is null by the choice-free translation invariance of
Lebesgue measure
([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]).

**Two warnings, part of the definition.** First, a difference quotient is
only defined on the shrunken set $\Omega_{i,h}$ inside $\Omega$, never on all
of $\Omega$; in particular it may be undefined on a strip of width $|h|$
along the boundary, so no estimate below differentiates a Sobolev class
across the boundary. Second, extending a class $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ by zero
does not enlarge the domain of its difference quotient: the quotient of the
extension agrees with $\delta_h^iu$ on $\Omega_{i,h}$, while values outside
$\Omega_{i,h}$ use points not both in $\Omega$ and are not values of the
original quotient. In the upper half-space, $\Omega_{n,h}=H$ for $h>0$,
whereas $\Omega_{n,h}=\{x\in H:x_n>|h|\}$ for $h<0$. This is why every
boundary argument on this page uses only
tangential quotients of compactly supported localisations, for which the
shrunken domain is the whole half-space and no extension across
$\partial\Omega$ is invoked.
items.strategy: Fix the shrunken domain $\Omega_{i,h}$, the translation sign convention of [[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]] and the class-level reading of quotients; the half-space statement records that tangential translations preserve $H$. The restriction to the shrunken set is what makes every later integration-by-parts identity well posed, and the Dirichlet warning is the reason the boundary proof may not differentiate in the normal direction ([H] Appendix 4.C, Definition 4.51, printed p. 124; [Si] Lecture 6 difference-quotient notation).

items.title: Difference-quotient calculus: integration by parts, product rule, commutation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$,
let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and fix $h\ne0$ and
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. Write
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ and
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\{x\in\Omega:x-he_i\in\Omega\}$
([[def-first-difference-quotient]]), so that
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\Omega_{i,h}+he_i$. Then:

(i) **Integration by parts, two-domain form.** Whenever the displayed
integrals converge absolutely,
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx+\frac1h\Big(\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx-\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx\Big).$$
Consequently, if
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx=\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx,$$
in particular if $uv$ vanishes almost everywhere outside
$\Omega_{i,h}\cap\Omega_{i,-h}$ — for instance when $uv$ has compact support in
$\Omega$ and $|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}(uv),\partial\Omega)$
— or if $\Omega_{i,h}=\Omega_{i,-h}$, then
$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx$,
with the integrals taken over their respective shrunken sets. For $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$
and $u\in L^p(\Omega)$, $v\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$p'$ the Hölder conjugate exponent of [[def-conjugate-exponents]]
($1/p+1/p'=1$), both sides are absolutely convergent and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx.$$

(ii) **Product rule.** If $uv\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, then a.e. on
$\Omega_{i,h}$,
$$\delta_h^i(uv)=\big(\tau_{-he_i}u\big)\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\,v=u\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\big(\tau_{-he_i}v\big),$$
with the translation $\tau_{-he_i}$ of [[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]].
The identity is a pointwise a.e. algebraic identity; no local integrability of
its shifted cross-products is asserted beyond the hypothesis $uv\in L^1_{\rm loc}$,
which makes the left side well defined.

(iii) **Commutation with weak derivatives.** If $u$ and all its weak
derivatives $D^\gamma u$ with $|\gamma|\le|\alpha|$ have locally integrable
representatives on $\Omega$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), then
$$D^\alpha(\delta_h^iu)=\delta_h^i(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{weakly on }\Omega_{i,h}.$$

All identities are identities of almost-everywhere classes
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and the proof uses no
choice beyond the Sobolev interfaces.
items.strategy: Change variables $x'=x+he_i$ in the first half of $\int\delta_h^iu\,v$ to obtain the negative of the $-h$ quotient, exactly as in [H] Proposition 4.52(2); the product rule is the algebraic identity $u_+v_+ -uv=(u_+-u)v+u_+(v_+-v)$ divided by $h$ ([H] Proposition 4.52(3)); weak commutation follows because the weak derivative and the translation commute and $\delta_h^i$ is a linear combination of two translations. The $L^p$/$L^{p'}$ version is the two-domain form of the identity together with Hölder ([L] equation (5.6) and the remarks around it, printed p. 108).

items.title: The cutoff difference-quotient commutator estimate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)$ with
$M_\eta:=\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}$ and compact support; the case
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is read by extending $\eta$ by zero.
Then for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every $h\ne0$, on the shrunken set
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ of
[[def-first-difference-quotient]] one has the exact identity
$$\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu=(\delta_h^i\eta)\,(\tau_{-he_i}u)\qquad\text{a.e. on }\Omega_{i,h},$$
where $\tau$ is the published translation $\tau_hu(x)=u(x-h)$ of
[[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]], so that
$(\tau_{-he_i}u)(x)=u(x+he_i)$. Consequently
$$\|\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|\tau_{-he_i}u\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
and more generally, on the domain where both sides are defined,
$$\delta_h^i\big(\eta^2\delta_h^iu\big)=\eta^2\delta_h^i\delta_h^iu+(\delta_h^i\eta^2)\,(\tau_{-he_i}\delta_h^iu).$$
The statement is quantitative in $\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty}$ and does not assume
any regularity of $u$ beyond $W^{1,p}$.
items.strategy: Apply the product rule (ii) of [[lem-difference-quotient-integration-by-parts]] to $\eta u$ and cancel $\eta\delta_h^iu$; the mean value inequality applied to $t\mapsto\eta(x+the_i)$ gives $|\delta_h^i\eta|\le M_\eta$, and $\tau_{he_i}$ preserves $L^p$ norms. The second identity is the same computation for $\eta^2$ and $\delta_h^iu$. This isolates the localisation error: the quotient of the localised function differs from the localisation of the quotient by a term containing the full derivative $D\eta$, which is what the absorption step of the interior estimate controls ([H] proof of Theorem 4.27, printed pp. 112-113; [Si] Lecture 6, properties (a)-(f) of the difference operators, printed pp. 60-61).

items.title: Uniformly bounded difference quotients represent a weak derivative
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega$ open, $1<p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$0<h_0<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)$. Suppose
$$\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C\qquad(0<|h|<h_0)$$
for every coordinate direction $i$. Then $u$ has a weak derivative
$D_iu\in L^p(\Omega')$ with $\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$, and for every
$\varphi\in L^{p'}(\Omega')$ one has
$\int_{\Omega'}\delta_h^iu\,\varphi\,dx\to\int_{\Omega'}D_iu\,\varphi\,dx$
as $h\to0$; consequently $\delta_h^iu\rightharpoonup D_iu$ weakly in
$L^p(\Omega')$. No weak compactness principle and no choice principle beyond
Countable Choice is used: the uniform bound makes the limit functional bounded
for every test function at once.
items.strategy: For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega'')$ with $\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ use integration by parts: $\int\delta_h^iu\,\varphi=-\int u\,\delta_{-h}^i\varphi$, and $\delta_{-h}^i\varphi\to\partial_i\varphi$ uniformly as $h\to0$ with the difference bounded by $\|D^2\varphi\|_\infty|h|$, so dominated convergence gives $\lim_h\int\delta_h^iu\,\varphi=-\int u\,\partial_i\varphi=:\ell(\varphi)$. The uniform bound and Hölder give $|\ell(\varphi)|\le C\|\varphi\|_{L^{p'}(\Omega')}$; since $C_c^\infty(\Omega')$ is dense in $L^{p'}(\Omega')$ (density of compactly supported continuous functions for Radon measures, upgraded by mollification), $\ell$ extends to a bounded functional on $L^{p'}(\Omega')$, and the sigma-finite duality theorem represents it by some $w\in L^p(\Omega')$ with $\|w\|_{L^p}\le C$. Then $\int u\,\partial_i\varphi=-\int w\varphi$ for every test function, so $D_iu=w$ and $\|D_iu\|\le C$. This is the conclusion of [H] Theorem 4.53(2) and [L] Proposition 5.7(ii) by a route that replaces their Banach-Alaoglu extraction by the duality representation.

items.title: The difference-quotient characterisation of $W^{1,p}$ for $1<p<\infty$
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$;
write $\delta_hu=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu)$ and
$Du=(D_1u,\dots,D_nu)$ for the difference-quotient and gradient vectors, with
$$\|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|\delta_h^iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega')},\qquad \|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|D_iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
(1) If $1\le p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, then for every
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)$ and every coordinate
direction $i$,
$$\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le n^{|1/p-1/2|}\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
At $p=2$ the vector estimate has constant one.
(2) Conversely, if $1<p<\infty$, $u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and there is $C$
with $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$ for every coordinate $i$ and all
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)/2$, then
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega')$ with $D_iu\in L^p(\Omega')$,
$\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$, and
$\delta_h^iu\rightharpoonup D_iu$ weakly in $L^p(\Omega')$ as $h\to0$.
Both parts are identities of classes and hold without any regularity of
$\partial\Omega$. At $p=1$ the converse in (2) is deliberately not asserted;
the companion remark records why only a measure derivative survives there.
items.strategy: Part (1) is the integral mean-value formula $u(x+he_i)-u(x)=h\int_0^1\partial_iu(x+the_i)\,dt$ for smooth $u$ followed by Jensen, Fubini and translation invariance, then density of smooth functions: this is [H] Theorem 4.53(1), [L] Proposition 5.7(i) and [Si] Lecture 5 Lemma 7. Part (2) is exactly [[lem-weak-limit-of-uniformly-bounded-difference-quotients-is-the-weak-derivative]]. The reflexive-range hypothesis $1<p<\infty$ is what makes the limit functional bounded in the dual exponent, and the $p=1$ exclusion is recorded by the companion remark ([H] Theorem 4.53, printed pp. 125-126; [L] Proposition 5.7, printed pp. 110-111).

items.title: At $p=1$ uniform difference-quotient bounds give only a measure derivative
items.statement:
The converse direction (2) of
[[thm-difference-quotient-characterisation-of-w-one-p-for-p-greater-than-one]]
is false at $p=1$ and is not asserted there. For the Heaviside step
$u=\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}$ on $\Omega=(-1,1)$ one has
$\delta_h^1u=h^{-1}\mathbf 1_{(-h,0)}$ on $\Omega_{1,h}=(-1,1-h)$ for $0<h<1$, so
$$\|\delta_h^1u\|_{L^1(\Omega_{1,h})}=1\qquad(0<h<1),$$
and likewise on any open $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega_{1,h}$ with
$(-h,0)\subseteq\Omega'$, while $u$ has no locally integrable weak derivative
([F2]); its
distributional derivative is the Dirac mass at $0$, and $u$ has bounded
variation on every compact subinterval of $\Omega$
([[def-bounded-variation-and-total-variation]]). Thus uniform local $L^1$
bounds on difference quotients yield, in the sharp form exhibited by this
witness, a finite measure derivative and a function of bounded variation, and
not membership in $W^{1,1}$. No consumer on this page may use part (2) at
$p=1$.
items.strategy: Compute $\delta_h^1u$ and its $L^1$ norm explicitly; the failure of $L^1$ weak differentiability is the published counterexample. The remark records the scope boundary of the characterisation theorem and the reason its proof in [[lem-weak-limit-of-uniformly-bounded-difference-quotients-is-the-weak-derivative]], which represents the limit in $L^{p'}$-duality, does not extend to $p=1$; the bounded-variation sharpening is cited, not used ([L] Proposition 5.7(ii) is stated for $1<p<\infty$; [H] Theorem 4.53(2) likewise, printed p. 125).

items.title: Local weak solutions of a divergence-form operator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev interfaces. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and not necessarily bounded, $n\ge1$,
let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $L$ and its sesquilinear
form $a$ be as in [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]], with
ellipticity constant $\theta$ and coefficient bounds $M_a,M_b,M_c$. Let
$f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

A class $u\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
([[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) is a **local weak solution of $Lu=f$ on
$\Omega$** if
$$a(u,v)=\int_\Omega f\,\overline v\,dx\qquad\text{for every }v\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K),$$
where $a$ is the sesquilinear form of
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] and the right-hand side is
finite because $v$ is bounded with compact support in $\Omega$ and
$f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.

**Equivalences and well-definedness.** Write $\Omega_2\Subset\Omega$ when
$\Omega_2$ is open, bounded and $\overline{\Omega_2}\subseteq\Omega$. For such
an $\Omega_2$ and $v\in H^1_0(\Omega_2)$ the class $v$ vanishes a.e. outside
$\Omega_2$, so
$a(u,v)$ and $\int_{\Omega_2}f\overline v$ are finite by
[[lem-elliptic-form-is-well-defined-and-bounded]] and Cauchy-Schwarz. The
defining identity for all $v\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ is equivalent to the
identity
$$a(u,v)=\int_{\Omega_2}f\,\overline v\,dx\qquad\text{for every bounded open }\Omega_2\Subset\Omega\text{ and every }v\in H^1_0(\Omega_2),$$
because $C_c^\infty(\Omega_2)$ is dense in $H^1_0(\Omega_2)$ by definition of
the closure ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and both sides are
continuous in $v$ in the $H^1(\Omega)$ norm: $a$ is bounded on $H^1(\Omega)$
by [[lem-elliptic-form-is-well-defined-and-bounded]], and
$|\int_{\Omega_2}f\overline v\,dx|\le\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega_2)}\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega_2)}$
by Cauchy-Schwarz, while the $H^1(\Omega_2)$ norm controls the $L^2(\Omega_2)$
norm. If in addition $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ then the defining identity is equivalent to
$a(u,v)=\int_\Omega f\overline v\,dx$ for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, since
$v\mapsto a(u,v)-\int_\Omega f\overline v$ is then bounded on the whole space
$H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ is dense in it. The definition
depends on $u$, on the coefficients and on $f$ only through their
almost-everywhere classes; this is the class-level statement of
[[lem-elliptic-form-is-well-defined-and-bounded]]. No boundary condition is
imposed, and the data class is $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$; this is strictly weaker
than the Dirichlet notion of [[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]],
which asks for $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ and a datum in the dual of $H^1_0$.

**Locality.** If $\Omega_0\subseteq\Omega$ is open and $u$ is a local weak
solution of $Lu=f$ on $\Omega$, then the restriction $u|_{\Omega_0}$ is a local
weak solution of $Lu=f|_{\Omega_0}$ on $\Omega_0$ with the same coefficient
functions restricted to $\Omega_0$: every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega_0)$
extends by zero to a test function of $\Omega$, and the defining integrals
over $\Omega$ are the integrals over $\Omega_0$ because $\varphi$ and all its
derivatives vanish outside $\Omega_0$. The equation is therefore a local
condition, which is why every regularity argument below may be localised to a
ball, a half-ball or a chart without changing the coefficients or the datum.

**The $H^1$ versus $H^1_0$ convention.** The solution is required to lie in
$H^1(\Omega)$ and the tests are required to vanish near $\partial\Omega$; this
is the interior formulation used in the regularity proof. Here
$H^1_0(\Omega_2)$ for a bounded $\Omega_2\Subset\Omega$ is the closure of
$C_c^\infty(\Omega_2)$ in the $H^1(\Omega_2)$ norm
([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), and all the
integrals are read in the class conventions of
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]].
items.strategy: This is the standard interior weak formulation used throughout the regularity proof; it differs from the Dirichlet definition only in dropping $u\in H^1_0$ and admitting $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ data, which is exactly what localisation by cutoffs produces. The identity is taken in the class vocabulary of [[lem-elliptic-form-is-well-defined-and-bounded]], and testing against $C_c^\infty$ is equivalent to testing against $H^1_0$ by the closure definition ([H] Section 4.11, (4.34)-(4.37), printed pp. 110-111; [T] Section 10.3, weak formulation (10.39)-(10.40), printed pp. 240-241).

items.title: The Caccioppoli inequality for weak elliptic solutions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with ellipticity constant
$\theta$ and coefficient bounds $M_a,M_b,M_c$, let
$f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and let $u\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be a
local weak solution of $Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). For every ball
$B_R(x_0)\Subset\Omega$ and every $0<r<R$ there is a constant
$C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c)$ with
$$\int_{B_r(x_0)}|Du|^2\,dx\le C\Big(\frac{1}{(R-r)^2}\int_{B_R(x_0)}|u|^2\,dx+\int_{B_R(x_0)}|u|^2\,dx+\int_{B_R(x_0)}|f|^2\,dx\Big).$$
No regularity of the coefficients beyond measurability and essential
boundedness is used, and the estimate is uniform in the localisation. When
$f=0$ the estimate is the energy inequality for a locally weak harmonic class.
items.strategy: Choose $\eta\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$ with $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ on $B_r(x_0)$ and $\|D\eta\|_\infty\le C/(R-r)$ ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], rescaled). Test the weak equation with $v=\eta^2u$, expand the three terms of $a(\eta^2u,u)$ (or of $a(u,\eta^2u)$), use uniform ellipticity on the principal part and Cauchy-Schwarz with Young's inequality on the first- and zero-order terms; the terms $\|\eta Du\|\|uD\eta\|$ and $\|\eta Du\|\|\eta u\|$ are absorbed into the left-hand side by the factor $\theta/2$, and the forcing term gives $\|\eta f\|\|\eta u\|$, again absorbed into $\|\eta u\|^2$ ([Si] Lecture 6, Lemma 1 and its proof, printed pp. 58-59; [H] proof of Theorem 4.27, the $v=\eta^2u$ step at the end, printed pp. 113-114).

items.title: Scaled Caccioppoli inequality on concentric balls
items.statement:
In the setting of [[thm-caccioppoli-inequality-for-weak-elliptic-solutions]],
for concentric balls $B_r(x_0)\Subset B_R(x_0)\Subset\Omega$ one has, with the
explicit scale,
$$\|Du\|^2_{L^2(B_r(x_0))}\le C\Big(\frac{1}{(R-r)^2}\|u\|^2_{L^2(B_R(x_0))}+\|u\|^2_{L^2(B_R(x_0))}+\|f\|^2_{L^2(B_R(x_0))}\Big),$$
where $C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c)$ does not depend on $r,R$ or on $x_0$. The
displayed $(R-r)^{-2}$ is the scale used in the nested-ball iteration; the
constants are not asserted to be sharp, and no claim is made as $r\to R$.
items.strategy: Insert into [[thm-caccioppoli-inequality-for-weak-elliptic-solutions]] a cutoff with the quantitative gradient bound $\|D\eta\|_\infty\le C/(R-r)$ supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], and collect the constants. The zero-order term is retained explicitly because it cannot be absorbed into the $(R-r)^{-2}$ term when $R-r\ge1$; this harmless term is controlled at the base of every iteration ([Si] Lecture 6, the constant $C(M,\theta,\rho,R,n)$ in Lemma 1, printed p. 59; [H] (4.39), printed p. 112).

items.title: The difference-quotient test function and its commutators
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.
(i) Let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$, $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. For every $0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}\eta,\partial\Omega)$
the class $v:=-\delta_{-h}^i\big(\eta^2\,\delta_h^iu\big)$
([[def-first-difference-quotient]]) is defined, has compact support in
$\Omega$, lies in $H^1(\Omega)$ and therefore in $H^1_0(\Omega)$
([[lem-compact-support-zero-extension-in-wkp]],
[[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). It is an admissible test class in the
weak equation of [[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]].
(ii) Let $H=\{x_n>0\}$ be the upper half-space,
$u\in H^1_0(H;\mathbb K)$ with $\operatorname{supp}u\subseteq B_1(0)\cap\overline H$,
$j<n$ a tangential index, and $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. Then for every fixed small $h\ne0$ the tangential class
$v:=-\delta_{-h}^j\big(\eta^2\,\delta_h^ju\big)$, read on $H$, lies in
$H^1_0(H)$: for each fixed $h$ the maps $w\mapsto\eta^2w$ and
$w\mapsto\delta_{\pm h}^jw$ are bounded on $H^1(H)$ and carry
$C_c^\infty(H)$ into itself, so they preserve the closure that defines
$H^1_0(H)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). In particular $v$ is admissible in a weak half-space problem whose datum defines a bounded functional on $H^1_0(H)$, including a datum in $L^2(H)$.
(iii) Fix the quotient direction $k$ (independent of the summed form indices $i,j$), put $w=\eta^2\delta_h^ku$ and $v=-\delta_{-h}^kw$. The principal pairing equals
$$\int\eta^2a^{ij}(x+he_k)\delta_h^kD_ju\overline{\delta_h^kD_iu}+R_{a,h},$$
where, writing $u_+=u(x+he_k)$ and using weak derivatives,
$$R_{a,h}=\int\eta^2(\delta_h^ka^{ij})D_ju\overline{\delta_h^kD_iu}+\int\left(a^{ij}(x+he_k)\delta_h^kD_ju+(\delta_h^ka^{ij})D_ju\right)\overline{D_i(\eta^2)\delta_h^ku}.$$
The full form adds the undifferentiated lower-order pairing $\int(b^iD_iu+cu)\overline v$. All these integrals are finite for each fixed admissible $h$, since bounded coefficient quotients have magnitude at most $2M_a/|h|$. If the principal coefficients have bounded first weak derivatives on the quotient neighbourhood, the principal remainder admits the usual Young bounds uniform in small $h$. No derivative or uniformly bounded difference quotient of $b,c$ is asserted or needed. The integrals are over the supported interior patch in case (i), and over $H$ in case (ii).
items.strategy: In (i), $u\in H^1$ gives $\delta_h^iu\in H^1$ with $D(\delta_h^iu)=\delta_h^i(Du)$ by the commutation rule of [[lem-difference-quotient-integration-by-parts]](iii), so $\eta^2\delta_h^iu\in H^1$ by the smooth-factor Leibniz rule ([[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]] and [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]), and the shifted quotient $\delta_{-h}^i$ preserves $H^1$ by the same commutation rule; the support lies in $(\operatorname{supp}\eta\cup(\operatorname{supp}\eta-he_i))$, a compact subset of $\Omega$ for small $h$, so the compact-support criterion of [[lem-compact-support-zero-extension-in-wkp]] applied to the interior gives membership in $H^1_0(\Omega)$. In (ii) the tangential shift preserves $H$, and since $u$ vanishes in $H^1_0$-norm against test functions supported near the boundary, the closure argument in the statement shows that both $\eta^2\delta_h^ju$ and its shifted quotient remain in $H^1_0(H)$ without any extension of $u$ across $\partial H$; the identities of (iii) are the expansions used in [H] (4.40)-(4.42) and in the boundary proof of Theorem 4.30, with the commutator terms controlled by [[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]] ([H] printed pp. 112-115; [T] proof of Lemma 10.18, printed p. 242; [Si] Lecture 9, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp. 88-90).

items.title: Localisation of a weak solution up to a bounded first-order term
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]], let
$f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak
solution of $Lu=f$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]) and let
$\zeta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Then $\zeta u\in H^1(\Omega)$ and
for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$
$$a(\zeta u,v)=\int_\Omega\zeta f\,\overline v\,dx+\int_\Omega a^{ij}(D_j\zeta)\,u\,\overline{D_iv}\,dx+\int_\Omega b^i u\,(D_i\zeta)\,\overline v\,dx-\int_\Omega a^{ij}(D_i\zeta)\,D_ju\,\overline v\,dx .$$
The three commutator terms are bounded by
$(2nM_a+\sqrt n M_b)\|D\zeta\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$ and
form a bounded sesquilinear form in $(u,v)$ with coefficients of first and
zero order bounded by $3nM_a\|D\zeta\|_\infty$ and $\sqrt n M_b\|D\zeta\|_\infty$,
while $\zeta f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with
$\|\zeta f\|_{L^2}\le\|\zeta\|_\infty\|f\|_{L^2(\operatorname{supp}\zeta)}$.
In particular a localised weak solution is a weak solution of the same
principal-part form with right-hand side $\zeta f$ in $L^2$ plus a bounded
first-order term, so it satisfies the Caccioppoli and difference-quotient
estimates of this page with constants depending only on
$n,M_a,M_b,M_c$ and $\|D\zeta\|_\infty$. The scaffold displayed only the
first two commutator terms; the term $-\int_\Omega a^{ij}(D_i\zeta)D_ju\overline v$
is required by the product rule, and the derivation below exhibits it.
items.strategy: Expand $D_j(\zeta u)=\zeta D_ju+uD_j\zeta$ and use the weak Leibniz rule [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]] (valid for $u\in H^1$) inside the form; the terms containing $\zeta$ reproduce $a(u,v)=\int f\overline v$ by the weak equation, and the remaining two terms are displayed. Boundedness follows from $a^{ij},b^i\in L^\infty$, $u,D\zeta\in L^2$ and Hölder, exactly as in [[lem-elliptic-form-is-well-defined-and-bounded]]. This is the localisation computation used in [Si] Lecture 6 (replace $u$ by $\zeta u$ in the differential equation) and in [T] proof of Lemma 10.18 (reduction to $u_j=\zeta_ju$), printed pp. 60-62 and 242.

items.title: Absorption of lower-order Sobolev terms in the elliptic estimate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $m\ge1$. For every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is $C=C(n,m,\varepsilon)$ such that every
$u\in H^{m+1}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ satisfies
$$\|D^mu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\,\|D^{m+1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C\,\|D^{m-1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)},$$
and the same estimate holds for every $u\in H^{m+1}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ whose
class vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact subset of $\Omega$. In
both displays
$$\|D^ju\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n,\,|\alpha|=j}\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 .$$
In particular, for $u\in H^2_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$,
$$\|Du\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\|D^2u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} .$$
The constants are not asserted sharp, and the estimate is the tool that
absorbs commutator terms linear in the highest derivatives.
items.strategy: For compactly supported smooth $u$ and each multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=m$, choose a coordinate $k$ with $\alpha_k\ge1$ and integrate by parts once: $\|D^\alpha u\|^2_{L^2}=-\int D^{\alpha+e_k}u\,\overline{D^{\alpha-e_k}u}\,dx$ (for complex $u$ integrate the conjugate factor), hence $\|D^\alpha u\|^2\le\|D^{m+1}u\|\,\|D^{m-1}u\|$; summing over the finitely many $\alpha$ and applying Young's inequality gives the claim, and the general class follows by density and closedness. This is the interpolation inequality of [Si] Lecture 5, Lemma 6 (stated there as $\|u\|_{m-1}\le\varepsilon\|u\|_m+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_0$), used in the improvement of the interior estimate to the $L^2$ norm on the right; [H] uses the scalar version inside the absorption step of the proof of Theorem 4.27.

items.title: Interior $H^2$ estimate for constant-coefficient elliptic equations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
let $a^{ij}\in\mathbb K$ be a constant matrix satisfying
$\operatorname{Re}\big(\sum a^{ij}\xi_j\overline{\xi_i}\big)\ge\theta|\xi|^2$
with $\theta>0$ and $|a^{ij}|\le M_a$, let $b^i,c\in\mathbb K$ be constants with $|b^i|\le M_b$,
$|c|\le M_c$, and let $L$ be the associated constant-coefficient
divergence-form operator with form $a$. Let $f\in L^2(B_R(x_0))$ and let
$u\in H^1(B_R(x_0))$ solve $Lu=f$ weakly on $B_R(x_0)$. Then
$u\in H^2(B_r(x_0))$ for every $0<r<R$, with
$$\|D^2u\|_{L^2(B_r(x_0))}\le C\Big(\left(1+\frac{1}{(R-r)^2}\right)\|u\|_{L^2(B_R(x_0))}+\|f\|_{L^2(B_R(x_0))}\Big),$$
where $C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c)$. No symmetry of $a$ and no boundary condition
on $u$ is required, and the estimate is the transparent constant-coefficient
core of the variable-coefficient theorem.
items.strategy: Choose a cutoff $\eta$ for $B_r\Subset B_R$ and test with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2\delta_h^ku)$, which is admissible by [[lem-tangential-difference-quotient-test-function]]. Because the $a^{ij}$ are constant, the principal term is exactly $\int\eta^2a^{ij}(\delta_h^k\partial_ju)\overline{(\delta_h^k\partial_iu)}$, bounded below by $\theta\|\eta\,\delta_h^kDu\|^2$; the constant lower-order terms commute with $\delta_h^k$ as well, and Cauchy-Schwarz with Young's inequality absorbs them into the left-hand side. This gives a uniform bound on $\|\eta\,\delta_h^kDu\|_{L^2}$, hence by [[thm-difference-quotient-characterisation-of-w-one-p-for-p-greater-than-one]](2) the existence of all second weak derivatives with the displayed estimate after [[lem-interpolation-absorbs-lower-order-sobolev-terms-in-elliptic-estimates]] replaces $\|Du\|_{L^2(B_R)}$ by $(R-r)^{-1}\|u\|_{L^2}$-type terms; the final elimination of $\|Du\|$ uses [[cor-scaled-caccioppoli-inequality-on-concentric-balls]]. This is the special case $L=-\Delta$ of [L] Theorem 5.6 and the local core of [H] Theorem 4.27 ([L] printed pp. 108-110; [H] printed pp. 110-114).

items.title: The differentiated weak equation with coefficient commutators
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$a^{ij}\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and
$b^i,c\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ with
$|a^{ij}|\le M_a$, $|b^i|\le M_b$, $|c|\le M_c$ and
$|D_ka^{ij}|,|D_kb^i|,|D_kc|\le M_1$ almost everywhere, let
$f\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$u\in H^1(\Omega)\cap H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a local weak solution of
$Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then for every
coordinate direction $k$ and every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, writing
$v:=D_ku\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), with
$f_k:=D_kf$, $\alpha^{ij}_k:=D_ka^{ij}$, $\beta^i_k:=D_kb^i$ and
$\gamma_k:=D_kc$,
$$\int_\Omega a^{ij}D_jv\,\overline{D_i\varphi}\,dx+\int_\Omega b^iD_iv\,\overline\varphi\,dx+\int_\Omega cv\,\overline\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega f_k\,\overline\varphi\,dx-\int_\Omega \alpha^{ij}_kD_ju\,\overline{D_i\varphi}\,dx-\int_\Omega \beta^i_kD_iu\,\overline\varphi\,dx-\int_\Omega \gamma_ku\,\overline\varphi\,dx .$$
Thus $v$ is a local weak solution of an equation with the same principal part
$a^{ij}$ and with bounded first- and zero-order coefficients; its datum
$g_k:=D_kf+D_i((D_ka^{ij})D_ju)-(D_kb^i)D_iu-(D_kc)u$ lies in
$L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. More generally, if $|\alpha|=j\ge1$,
$u\in H^{j+1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $f\in H^j_{\mathrm{loc}}$,
$a^{ij}\in W^{j+1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and $b^i,c\in
W^{j,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, then $D^\alpha u$ solves the same-principal-part
equation with datum
$$g_\alpha:=D^\alpha f+\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}D_i\!\left((D^\beta a^{ij})D_jD^{\alpha-\beta}u\right)-\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}\left((D^\beta b^i)D_iD^{\alpha-\beta}u+(D^\beta c)D^{\alpha-\beta}u\right)\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega).$$
The principal coefficient derivatives through order $j+1$ ensure that the
divergence commutators are genuine $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ functions, not merely
$H^{-1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ functionals. The scaffold assumed only $u\in H^1(\Omega)$; the integral defining
$\int a^{ij}D_jv\overline{D_i\varphi}$ requires $v\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$,
equivalently $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, which is the regularity
available in every induction step that consumes this lemma.
items.strategy: Replace $\varphi$ by $-D_k\varphi$ in the weak identity and integrate by parts in $x_k$; all terms are absolutely convergent because $Du\in L^2$ and the coefficient derivatives are bounded ([T] proof of Corollary 10.17: the identity $a(v,\partial_lu)=\langle v,\tilde f\rangle$ with $\tilde f=\partial_l(f-\sum b_j\partial_ju-cu)-\sum\partial_i(\partial_lA)\partial_ju$, printed p. 241; [H] the formal differentiation of the equation before Theorem 4.28, printed p. 114). The lemma displays the commutators $D_ka^{ij}D_ju$ so that no consumer claims that a derivative of a weak solution solves the identical equation.

items.title: Interior $H^2$ regularity for divergence-form equations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$n\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with constants
$\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c$ and with $a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ satisfying
$\|Da^{ij}\|_\infty\le M_1$, and let $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of $Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for all open sets
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ there is
$C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,M_1,\Omega',\Omega'')$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega')}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}\big).$$
Consequently the equation $Lu=f$ holds pointwise almost everywhere with
$D_i(a^{ij}D_ju)$ understood through the a.e. defined product
$(D_ia^{ij})D_ju+a^{ij}D_iD_ju$, and the same estimate holds for complex-valued $u$ by taking real parts in the coercive energy bounds; no splitting of complex coefficients into real and imaginary equations is used.
The scaffold wrote $\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ on the
right-hand side, which is ill-posed for a datum known only to lie in
$L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ (for instance $f=1/x$ on $\Omega=(0,1)$ is
locally but not globally square-integrable); the nested formulation above is
the well-posed local statement, and the quantitative content is otherwise
unchanged.
items.strategy: Use the test function of [[lem-tangential-difference-quotient-test-function]] and isolate the principal term; the coefficient commutator $D_ka^{ij}D_ju$ is controlled by $M_1\|Du\|$ and absorbed with the interpolation inequality of [[lem-interpolation-absorbs-lower-order-sobolev-terms-in-elliptic-estimates]] into $\varepsilon\|\eta\delta_h^kDu\|^2$ plus $C_\varepsilon\|u\|^2_{L^2}$; this yields a bound on $\|\eta\delta_h^kDu\|$ uniform in $h$, and [[thm-difference-quotient-characterisation-of-w-one-p-for-p-greater-than-one]](2) produces $D_kDu\in L^2(\Omega')$. The interior estimate with the $L^2$ norm of $u$ on the right follows by first taking $\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ and then testing the equation with $\eta^2u$ ([[lem-localisation-identity-for-a-divergence-form-weak-solution]] and [H]'s final step). The a.e. strong form follows because the difference $g:=f-(-D_i(a^{ij}D_ju)+b^iD_iu+cu)\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ pairs trivially with every test function, and $C_c^\infty$ is dense in $L^2$ ([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-ltwo-of-an-open-set]]). Constant coefficients are the core case [[thm-interior-h-two-estimate-for-constant-coefficient-elliptic-equations]]; the general proof is [H] Theorem 4.27, [L] Theorem 5.6 and [T] Lemma 10.16 ([H] printed pp. 110-114; [L] printed pp. 108-110; [T] printed pp. 240-241).

items.title: Nested-domain induction for interior elliptic derivatives
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $k\ge0$,
let $a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega)$, $b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ with
bounds $|D^\ell a^{ij}|\le M_\ell$ for $|\ell|\le k+1$ and
$|D^\ell b^i|,|D^\ell c|\le M_\ell$ for $|\ell|\le k$ almost everywhere, let
$f\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak
solution of $Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Fix open sets
$\Omega_{-1},\Omega_0,\Omega_1,\dots,\Omega_{k+1}$ with
$\overline{\Omega_{-1}}\Subset\Omega$, $\overline{\Omega_0}\Subset\Omega_{-1}$
and $\overline{\Omega_{j+1}}\Subset\Omega_j$ for $0\le j\le k$. Then for every
$0\le j\le k$ one has $u\in H^{j+2}(\Omega_j)$, and there is a constant $C_j$
depending only on $n,\theta,k$, the principal-coefficient bounds through
order $j+1$, the lower-order coefficient bounds through order $j$, and the sets
$\Omega_{-1},\dots,\Omega_j$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^{j+2}(\Omega_j)}\le C_j\big(\|f\|_{H^j(\Omega_{-1})}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega_{-1})}\big).$$
The induction step is: each weak derivative $D^\alpha u$ of order $|\alpha|=j$
solves on $\Omega_{j-1}$ the iterated differentiated equation of
[[lem-weak-equation-for-a-first-derivative-includes-coefficient-commutators]]
with datum in $L^2(\Omega_{j-1})$ built from $D^jf$, principal coefficient
derivatives through order $j+1$, and derivatives of $u$ of order at most
$j+1$, so the interior $H^2$ theorem applied on
$\Omega_j\Subset\Omega_{j-1}$ recovers two further derivatives; the loss of
domain is absorbed into the fixed chain. The scaffold wrote $\Omega=\Omega_0$
and concluded $u\in H^{j+2}(\Omega_0)$ at $j=0$, which would be a global
$H^2(\Omega)$ claim and is false for an arbitrary local weak solution; the
outer set $\Omega_{-1}\Subset\Omega$ is the localisation needed for the
interior estimates, and all constants below depend on it.
items.strategy: Induct on $j$. For $j=0$ this is [[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]] on $\Omega_1$. For the step, apply the induction hypothesis to $v=D_lu$ on the shifted sequence $\Omega_1\Supset\cdots\Supset\Omega_{j+1}$ using the differentiated equation of [[lem-weak-equation-for-a-first-derivative-includes-coefficient-commutators]]; the coefficient bounds of order $j+1$ for $u$'s equation control those of $v$'s equation. This is the fixed-nested-cutoff bookkeeping of [H] Theorem 4.28 (via [9] there) and [Si] Lecture 6, Theorem 1, whose constant depends on the fixed balls but not on the number of steps ([H] printed p. 114; [Si] printed pp. 60-63).

items.title: Interior $H^{k+2}$ elliptic regularity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $k\ge0$, and let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$,
$b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, all derivatives bounded by
constants $M_\ell$; let $f\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and let
$u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak solution of $Lu=f$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then
$u\in H^{k+2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for all open sets
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ there is
$C=C(n,\theta,k,M_0,\dots,M_{k+1},\Omega',\Omega'')$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}(\Omega')}\le C\big(\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega'')}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}\big).$$
The gain is exactly two derivatives; the coefficient regularity required is
one order above the data order. For $k=0$ the theorem reduces to
[[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]]. The
scaffold wrote $\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ on the right-hand
side, which is ill-posed for locally Sobolev data on an unbounded $\Omega$;
the nested formulation is the well-posed local statement.
items.strategy: The induction is [[lem-nested-domain-induction-for-interior-elliptic-derivatives]]: $H^{k+2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is local, so fix $\Omega'\Subset\Omega_{k+1}$ in a nested chain and read the estimate off the chain. This is [H] Theorem 4.28, [L] Theorem 5.8 and [T] Corollary 10.17 ([H] printed p. 114; [L] printed p. 111; [T] printed pp. 240-241). The lower-order coefficients are allowed to be only $W^{k,\infty}$ on the open set, as in [T]; no boundary condition on $u$ is used.

items.title: Smooth data give smooth interior solutions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the Sobolev embedding used in the last step,
and Countable Choice for the Sobolev interfaces. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb
R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and suppose
the coefficients $a^{ij},b^i,c$ and the datum $f$ are of class
$C^\infty(\Omega)$. If $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of
$Lu=f$ on $\Omega$ ([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]),
then $u\in H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for every $m\in\mathbb N$, and
consequently $u$ agrees almost everywhere with a function of class
$C^\infty(\Omega)$, for which $Lu=f$ holds pointwise in $\Omega$. No
boundary condition is imposed, and the conclusion is interior only.
items.strategy: Apply [[thm-interior-h-k-plus-two-elliptic-regularity]] for every $k$ on compactly contained subsets; each step legitimises the next because the coefficients are $C^\infty$ and $f$ has all local Sobolev orders. Then choose $m$ with $m>n/2$ and apply the higher-order Sobolev embedding and Morrey's inequality on a ball $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$ to obtain derivatives of $u$ up to any fixed order $\ell$ as continuous functions; since $\ell$ is arbitrary, the continuous representative is $C^\infty$ and the a.e. equation becomes pointwise. This is [H] Corollary 4.29 and [L] Theorem 5.9; the embedding step inherits the Axiom of Choice recorded by [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] ([H] printed p. 114; [L] printed p. 112).

items.title: Weak divergence-form equations are invariant under $C^2$ boundary charts
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]], let $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak solution of $Lu=f$ ([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Let $\Phi:W\to V$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism of ambient open sets such that $\Phi(W\cap\Omega)=V\cap H$, where $H=\{y_n>0\}$, and put $\psi=\Phi^{-1}$. Then $\widehat u=u\circ\psi\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(V\cap H)$, with
$$D\widehat u(y)=D\psi(y)^TDu(\psi(y)),$$
and it solves $\widehat L\widehat u=\widehat f$ locally weakly, where $\widehat f=|\det D\psi|(f\circ\psi)$ and
$$\widetilde a^{ij}(y)=|\det D\psi(y)|\sum_{p,q}a^{pq}(\psi(y))\partial_p\Phi_i(\psi(y))\partial_q\Phi_j(\psi(y)),$$
$$\widetilde b^i(y)=|\det D\psi(y)|\sum_pb^p(\psi(y))\partial_p\Phi_i(\psi(y)),\qquad \widetilde c(y)=|\det D\psi(y)|c(\psi(y)).$$
The transformed datum is locally $L^2$, and the transformed coefficients are locally bounded; quantitative ellipticity is given by the companion flattening lemma. If $\zeta\in C_c^\infty(W)$ is an ambient cutoff, then $\widehat{\zeta u}\in H^1(V\cap H)$, with a norm bound determined by the cutoff and the chart/inverse derivative and Jacobian bounds on a compact ambient neighbourhood of $\operatorname{supp}\zeta$. Its distributional transformed equation uses the localized datum; when $a\in W^{1,\infty}$ and the original datum is square-integrable on the localized patch, that localized datum is also $L^2$. If additionally $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, then $\widehat{\zeta u}\in H^1_0(V\cap H)$, so zero Dirichlet data are preserved. In particular these global and zero-trace conclusions hold for $u$ itself when its support in $\overline\Omega$ is a compact subset of $W$, by choosing $\zeta=1$ near that support. The change of variables acts on the weak formulation and requires no classical regularity of $u$.
items.strategy: First prove the pullback membership: on a compactly contained open set approximate $u$ in $H^1$ by interior mollifications ([density of $C_c^\infty$ in $H^1$ of an open set], the convolution-derivative theorem and the commutation of mollification with weak derivatives), pull the smooth approximations back with the chain rule, and pass to the limit using the uniform bounds on $D\psi$, $|\det D\psi|$ and $|\det D\Phi|$ over compact subsets; this yields $\widehat u\in H^1$ with the displayed a.e. gradient. Then test the transformed equation against $\widehat v=v\circ\Phi$ for $v\in C_c^\infty(V\cap H)$ and use the change-of-variables formula for Lipschitz maps and the chain rule to identify the coefficient formulas exactly as in [H]'s computation for $\widetilde a^{\,ij}$ ([H] Section 4.12, printed p. 114); the term $|\det D\psi|$ and the shifts of the first-order coefficients $b^i$ are the ones forced by the substitution. The lemma is the PDE-18 addition that separates weak-form legitimacy from ellipticity preservation.

items.title: $C^2$ flattening preserves uniform ellipticity quantitatively
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. In the setting of
[[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]]
with $W$ compactly contained in the domain of a flattening chart of a bounded
$C^2$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), suppose
$\Lambda\ge1$ bounds $|D\Phi|,|D\psi|,|\det D\Phi|$ and $|\det D\psi|$
together with their reciprocals on the relevant closure:
$\Lambda^{-1}\le|\det D\psi(y)|\le\Lambda$ and
$|\zeta|\le\Lambda|D\Phi(y)\zeta|$ for all $\zeta$. Then the transformed
coefficients $\widetilde a^{\,ij}$ of
[[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]]
satisfy, for a.e. $y$ in the flattened half-ball,
$$\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}\widetilde a^{ij}(y)\xi_j\overline{\xi_i}\ \ge\ \theta\,\Lambda^{-2}\inf|\det D\psi|\ |\xi|^2\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb C^n),$$
so the transformed operator is uniformly elliptic with an explicitly
computable constant depending only on $n,\theta,\Lambda$ and the ellipticity
angle, while the transformed coefficients satisfy
$|\widetilde a^{\,ij}|\le n^2M_a\Lambda^3$. The first-order and zero-order
coefficients satisfy $|\widetilde b^{\,i}|\le nM_b\Lambda^2$ and
$|\widetilde c|\le M_c\Lambda$, hence also the scaffold's non-sharp bounds
$C(n)(M_a+M_b)\Lambda^3$ for $|\widetilde b^{\,i}|$ and
$C(n)(M_a+M_b+M_c)\Lambda^3$ for $|\widetilde c|$, since $\Lambda\ge1$.
The constants are not asserted sharp.
items.strategy: Insert $\zeta=(D\Phi^{T})\xi$, i.e. $\zeta_p=\sum_i\partial_p\varphi_i\,\xi_i$, into the ellipticity inequality for $a$ at $\psi(y)$ and use $|\det D\psi|>0$ together with the two-sided bound on $D\Phi$; this is the computation performed in [H] Section 4.12 immediately after the coefficient formulas, where the chain rule expresses $\sum_{i,j}\widetilde a^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j=|\det D\psi|\sum_{p,q}a^{pq}\zeta_p\zeta_q$, and where the remark that $C^2$ boundary is needed for $\widetilde a^{\,ij}$ to be $C^1$ (i.e. $W^{1,\infty}$) appears ([H] printed p. 114; [L] boundary-regularity proof sketch, printed p. 113; [T] proof of Lemma 10.18, printed p. 242).

items.title: Tangential $H^2$ estimate near a flat Dirichlet boundary
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $H=\{x_n>0\}$ be the upper half-space, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(H)$, $b^i,c\in L^\infty(H)$ and bounds
$\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,M_1$, let $f\in L^2(H)$, and let $u\in H^1_0(H)$ be
supported in $B_1(0)\cap\overline H$ and solve $Lu=f$ weakly on $H$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then for every
tangential index $k<n$ and every $i$ the weak derivative $D_kD_iu$ belongs
to $L^2(B_{1/2}(0)\cap H)$ with
$$\sum_{k<n}\sum_{i=1}^n\int_{B_{1/2}(0)\cap H}|D_kD_iu|^2\,dx\le C\big(\|f\|^2_{L^2(H)}+\|u\|^2_{L^2(H)}\big),$$
where $C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,M_1)$ is independent of the step size. Only
tangential difference quotients of $u$ are used, so no extension of $u$
across the boundary is invoked.
items.strategy: Test the weak equation with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2\delta_h^ku)$ for a tangential index $k<n$; by [[lem-tangential-difference-quotient-test-function]] this class is compactly supported in $H$ and lies in $H^1_0(H)$. Because the shift is tangential, the test function stays in $H^1_0(H)$ by part (ii) of [[lem-tangential-difference-quotient-test-function]] and the principal term is the uniformly elliptic quadratic form in $\delta_h^kDu$; the coefficient commutators are controlled by [[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]] and absorbed by [[lem-interpolation-absorbs-lower-order-sobolev-terms-in-elliptic-estimates]], and the forcing term is bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz. The resulting bound on $\|\eta\delta_h^kDu\|_{L^2}$ is uniform in $h$, and [[lem-weak-limit-of-uniformly-bounded-difference-quotients-is-the-weak-derivative]] identifies the limit as $D_kDu$. This is the first half of the proof of [H] Theorem 4.30 and of [T] Lemma 10.18, and the content of the boundary lemma of [Si] Lecture 8 ([H] printed p. 115; [T] printed p. 242; [Si] printed pp. 82-85).

items.title: The normal second derivative is recovered from the equation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$ and give $\mathbb R^n$ its Euclidean metric
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Define the open half-space
$H:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ and its boundary hyperplane
$\partial H=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_n=0\}$. For $r>0$, write
$B_r(x_0):=\{x:|x-x_0|<r\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), so the boundary
half-ball is $Q=\{x:|x-x_0|<r,\ x_n>0\}$ with $(x_0)_n=0$. Let
$u\in H^1_0(H)\cap H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ be such that the tangential second
derivatives $D_kD_iu$ ($k<n$) and the derivatives $D_nD_iu$ for $i<n$ exist
in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$; suppose $u$ solves $Lu=f$ weakly on $H$ with
$a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(H)$ uniformly elliptic with constant $\theta$,
$b^i,c\in L^\infty(H)$ and $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then the
missing normal derivative $D_nD_nu$ exists in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ and
satisfies throughout $H$, in the almost-everywhere strong form,
$$D_nD_nu=\frac{1}{a^{nn}}\Big(-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}a^{ij}D_iD_ju-\sum_{i,j}(D_ia^{ij})D_ju+b^iD_iu+cu-f\Big)$$
almost everywhere, with the pointwise bound
$|D_nD_nu|\le\theta^{-1}(M_a\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}|D_iD_ju|+C(n)(M_1+M_b)|Du|+M_c|u|+|f|)$
and the corresponding $L^2$ estimate on each boundary half-ball $Q=B_r(x_0)\cap H$, $x_0\in\partial H$, on which $f$ and all the nonnormal second derivatives on the right are in $L^2(Q)$. In particular those hypotheses imply $D_n^2u\in L^2(Q)$, with
$$\|D_n^2u\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C\left(\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}\|D_iD_ju\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|Du\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|u\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|f\|_{L^2(Q)}\right).$$
Uniform ellipticity gives $\operatorname{Re}a^{nn}\ge\theta$ and hence $|a^{nn}|\ge\theta$, which makes division legitimate for real or complex coefficients.
items.strategy: Once $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the weak identity tested against $\varphi\in C_c^\infty$ holds with the strong expression, so the distributional identity $a^{nn}D_nD_nu=-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}a^{ij}D_iD_ju-\sum_{i,j}(D_ia^{ij})D_ju+b^iD_iu+cu-f$ holds on the region where the right-hand side is in $L^2$; solving for the normal derivative uses $a^{nn}\ge\theta$ from ellipticity with $\xi=e_n$. This is the second half of [H] Theorem 4.30, of [T] Lemma 10.18 and of [L] Theorem 5.10's proof sketch ([H] printed pp. 115-116; [T] printed p. 242; [L] printed p. 113).

items.title: A finite partition glues the local interior and boundary $H^2$ estimates
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^2$
domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), $n\ge2$, let $L,a$
be as in [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$, $b^i,c\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, and let
$f\in L^2(\Omega)$. Suppose $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of
$Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]) and suppose the
following local bounds are available: an interior bound on a fixed open set
$U_0\Subset\Omega$, and, for finitely many boundary charts $(W_\ell,\Phi_\ell)$
covering $\partial\Omega$, a bound for the flattened localisations
$\widehat{(\zeta_\ell u)}$ in $H^2$ of the flattened half-balls in the
variables of
[[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]],
each with the bounds of
[[lem-c-two-boundary-flattening-transforms-uniform-ellipticity]]. Then
$u\in H^2(\Omega)$ and there is $C$, depending only on
$n,\Omega,\theta$ and the coefficient bounds, with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big).$$
The proof uses a finite smooth partition of unity subordinate to the cover,
the localisation identities of
[[lem-localisation-identity-for-a-divergence-form-weak-solution]], and the
finiteness of the cover; no choice of a cover beyond the finite chart
neighbourhoods supplied by the definition is used.
items.strategy: Cover $\overline\Omega$ by the interior set $U_0$ and finitely many chart neighbourhoods $W_\ell$ (compactness of $\overline\Omega$ and the finite boundary atlas of the definition). Choose a finite smooth partition of unity $\{\zeta_\ell\}$ subordinate to this cover with compact supports using [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]]. Each $\zeta_\ell u$ satisfies the localisation identity of [[lem-localisation-identity-for-a-divergence-form-weak-solution]]; on the interior piece apply [[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]], on each boundary piece flatten by [[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]] (with ellipticity from [[lem-c-two-boundary-flattening-transforms-uniform-ellipticity]]) and apply the tangential estimate of [[lem-tangential-h-two-estimate-near-a-flat-dirichlet-boundary]] together with the normal recovery of [[lem-normal-second-derivative-recovered-from-the-elliptic-equation]]; sum the finitely many estimates. This is the globalisation step of [H] Section 4.12, [T] proof of Lemma 10.18 and [Si] Lecture 9 ([H] printed p. 115; [T] printed pp. 242-243; [Si] printed pp. 88-90).

items.title: Global $H^2$ Dirichlet regularity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^2$
domain, $n\ge2$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with ellipticity
constant $\theta$, bounds $M_a,M_b,M_c$ and $a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$,
$b^i,c\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of $Lu=f$ with zero boundary values
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^2(\Omega)$ and there is
$C=C(n,\Omega,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,\|Da^{ij}\|_\infty)$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big).$$
The $L^2$ norm of $u$ on the right cannot be deleted without a hypothesis
excluding the homogeneous kernel, as the companion counterexample shows; the
theorem is stated for zero Dirichlet data, and nonzero compatible boundary
data are handled by a trace lifting before the theorem is applied.
items.strategy: Combine [[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]] for the interior piece with the flat-boundary tangential estimate and normal recovery, glued by [[lem-finite-boundary-and-interior-partition-glues-local-h-two-estimates]]. The Dirichlet condition $u\in H^1_0$ is used only to keep the localisation of $u$ admissible after flattening and to control the support of the tangential test functions; no trace operator is invoked. items.title: The global $H^2$ estimate without the $L^2$ term under uniqueness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. In the setting of
[[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]] suppose that the homogeneous
problem has only the trivial solution: $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ and
$a(u,v)=0$ for all $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ imply $u=0$. Then for every
$f\in L^2(\Omega)$ the unique weak solution $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ of $Lu=f$
satisfies $u\in H^2(\Omega)$ and there is
$C=C(n,\Omega,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,\|Da^{ij}\|_\infty,
\|L^{-1}\|_{\mathcal L(L^2(\Omega),H^1_0(\Omega))})$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
Thus the $L^2$ term may be dropped exactly under the injectivity hypothesis,
and the estimate is uniform over all data.
items.strategy: Triviality of the homogeneous kernel excludes the second alternative of the Fredholm alternative of [[thm-fredholm-alternative-for-weak-elliptic-dirichlet-problems]], so the first alternative holds and the solution map $f\mapsto u$ is bounded from $L^2(\Omega)$ to $H^1_0(\Omega)$ by [[cor-uniqueness-implies-existence-for-the-elliptic-dirichlet-problem]]; combining $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C\|f\|$ with the estimate of [[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]] gives the claim. The design's alternative contradiction argument uses the Rellich compactness of $H^1_0(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega)$: a sequence with $\|u_k\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|f_k\|_{L^2}\to0$ converges weakly in $H^1$ and strongly in $L^2$ along a subsequence to a nontrivial homogeneous solution, contradiction; the scaffold uses the equivalent formalised compactness statement of the Fredholm page so that the compactness content is proved once ([H] Theorem 4.24 and its use of the compact resolvent, printed pp. 106-108).

items.title: Higher-order boundary regularity for Dirichlet problems
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded
$C^{k+2}$ domain, $n\ge2$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$k\ge0$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega)$, $b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ and all
coefficient derivatives bounded, and let $f\in H^k(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of $Lu=f$ with zero boundary values
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^{k+2}(\Omega)$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}(\Omega)}\le C\big(\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big),$$
with $C$ depending only on $n,k,\Omega$ and the coefficient bounds. The
derivative gain is exactly two orders; the boundary regularity required at
order $k$ is $C^{k+2}$, the coefficient regularity one order above the data
order, and the companion page records the sharp two-derivative example. For
$k=0$ the theorem is
[[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]].
items.strategy: Localise with the finite partition as in [[lem-finite-boundary-and-interior-partition-glues-local-h-two-estimates]]; after flattening, apply the tangential difference-quotient estimate to derivatives $D_lu$ of increasing order, each of which continues to vanish on the boundary (tangential derivatives preserve $H^1_0$ and the compact support of the localisations), then recover the highest normal derivative from the differentiated equation of [[lem-weak-equation-for-a-first-derivative-includes-coefficient-commutators]] exactly as in [[lem-normal-second-derivative-recovered-from-the-elliptic-equation]]. The coefficient regularity needed at each step is one order above the corresponding data order, and the boundary must be $C^{k+2}$ so that the flattened coefficients retain the required $W^{k+1,\infty}$ regularity. This is [H] Theorem 4.31, [L] Theorem 5.11, [T] Corollary 10.19 and [Si] Lecture 9, Theorem 1 ([H] printed p. 116; [L] printed p. 113; [T] printed pp. 242-243; [Si] printed pp. 86-90).

items.title: Smooth weak Dirichlet solutions are classical
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (for the Sobolev embedding and the trace
characterisation) and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^\infty$ domain, $n\ge2$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
and suppose $a^{ij},b^i,c,f$ extend to $C^\infty$ functions on a
neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$. If $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak
solution of $Lu=f$ with zero boundary values
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^m(\Omega)$ for every $m$; $u$ agrees almost everywhere with a
function $\widetilde u\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ satisfying $Lu=f$
pointwise in $\Omega$, and $\widetilde u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$. The boundary
values are those of the continuous representative, consistent with the trace
characterisation of [[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]]; the
statement asserts no pointwise boundary condition for the Sobolev class
itself.
items.strategy: Apply [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]] for every $k$ with the smooth coefficients; the bootstrapping is legitimate because each step improves the data order. Then use the higher-order Sobolev embedding and Morrey's inequality on $\Omega$ to obtain a representative with continuous derivatives of every fixed order, so the representative is $C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$; the a.e. equation is then pointwise. Finally, the continuous representative has trace equal to its boundary restriction, and since $u\in H^1_0$ has zero trace, that restriction vanishes ([[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]]). This is [H] Corollary 4.32 and [L] Theorem 5.11 ([H] printed p. 116; [L] printed p. 113).

items.title: Smooth coefficients and boundary make elliptic eigenfunctions smooth
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (inherited through
[[cor-smooth-weak-dirichlet-solutions-are-classical]]) and Countable Choice.
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, $n\ge2$, and
let $a^{ij},b^i,c$ extend to $C^\infty$ functions on a neighbourhood of
$\overline\Omega$, with $a$ symmetric and uniformly elliptic. If
$(\lambda,u)$ is a symmetric elliptic weak eigenpair
([[def-symmetric-elliptic-weak-eigenpair]]), $a(u,v)=\lambda(u,v)_{L^2}$ for
all $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $u\neq0$, then $u\in H^m(\Omega)$ for every
$m$, and $u$ agrees almost everywhere with a function
$\widetilde u\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ satisfying
$L\widetilde u=\lambda\widetilde u$ pointwise in $\Omega$ and
$\widetilde u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$. This is the relocated PDE-17
consequence: the spectral construction needs only weak eigenfunctions, and
smoothness is supplied here by the regularity theory.
items.strategy: The weak eigenequation is the weak Dirichlet problem $Lu=\lambda u$ with datum $\lambda u$; start from $u\in H^1_0\subset L^2$ and iterate [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]]: $u\in H^2$ makes $\lambda u\in H^2$, hence $u\in H^4$, and so on. Apply [[cor-smooth-weak-dirichlet-solutions-are-classical]] to conclude. The statement and proof route are preserved from the PDE-17 owner resolution, which moved this corollary after the PDE-18 higher-order boundary regularity and embedding items; the item records no new spectral input ([H] Sections 4.10-4.12, printed pp. 108-116; [Si] Lectures 9-10).

items.title: Regularity estimates do not create boundary compatibility
items.statement:
Under the choice assumptions of the cited Sobolev trace interfaces
(the Axiom of Choice), the global $H^2$ and higher-order boundary theorems of this page
([[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]],
[[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]]) take the
solution in $H^1_0(\Omega)$, equivalently with zero trace, or apply after subtracting a lifting of the same Sobolev order as the
regularity sought, with the resulting forcing in the required data space.
An $H^1$ lifting alone does not supply an $H^2$ or higher-order estimate. They are a priori estimates, not existence
or compatibility statements: they cannot manufacture boundary regularity for
a datum that is not the trace of an $H^s$ function. On a nonsmooth domain
with a corner, smooth coefficients and boundary data on each open boundary
piece do not remove the corner obstruction. In the
inhomogeneous weak Dirichlet problem the datum must lie in the trace range
and be lifted before the estimates apply
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]],
[[cor-inhomogeneous-weak-dirichlet-problem-by-a-trace-lifting]]); the
companion examples of this pair's examples page show two smooth boundary
pieces with no solution continuous on the closure, and show that the $C^2$
boundary hypothesis itself cannot be dropped. No proof is supplied here; the
remark records the scope boundary of the estimates.
items.strategy: Record the scope: the estimates quantify already-compatible solutions, and the lifting of PDE-16 is the mechanism that turns an admissible boundary datum into the zero-trace problem. Point to the B-companion counterexamples for the failure modes ([H] Section 4.12 statement hypotheses, printed pp. 114-116; [T] Example 10.1, printed p. 242).

items.title: Poisson's equation with $L^2$ data gains two interior derivatives
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice where the existence of the weak solution is
invoked; the regularity conclusion itself uses only Countable Choice. Let
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded open set, let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, and
let $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ be a weak solution of the Dirichlet problem
$-\Delta u=f$, that is, $a(u,v)=\int_\Omega f\overline v\,dx$ for every
$v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $a(u,v)=\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\overline{\nabla v}\,dx$
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Assuming the
Axiom of Choice, existence and uniqueness of such a $u$ are supplied by
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-for-the-weak-dirichlet-poisson-problem]] when
$\Omega$ is nonempty; if $\Omega=\varnothing$, the zero class is the unique
weak solution directly. The verification below uses only that $u$ is a weak
solution. Then
$u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for every open
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega$ there is $C=C(n,\Omega',\Omega)$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega')}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big):$$
$L^2$ data gain two interior derivatives for the constant-coefficient
Laplacian, and no boundary regularity of $\Omega$ enters the interior
conclusion.
items.strategy: Instantiate the interior H^2 theorem with L=-Delta, whose coefficients are constant and uniformly elliptic. A zero-trace weak solution is a local weak solution. For each Omega' compactly contained in Omega choose Omega'' with Omega' compactly contained in Omega'' compactly contained in Omega, apply the nested-domain estimate, then bound its local data norms by the global norms. Existence is cited only for nonempty Omega and uses AC; the empty-domain solution and estimate are direct.

items.title: A piecewise-smooth coefficient gives an $H^2$ solution that is not twice classically differentiable
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(-1,1)$ let
$$a(x)=\begin{cases}2+x,&x<0,\\ 2+2x,&x>0,\end{cases}$$
a continuous, piecewise smooth coefficient with $1\le a\le4$ and
$a\in W^{1,\infty}(-1,1)$ whose derivative jumps from $1$ to $2$ at $0$, and
define $u(x)=\int_0^x\frac{dt}{a(t)}$, the absolutely continuous primitive
with $u(0)=0$. Then $u\in H^2(-1,1)$, the flux is $au'\equiv1$, and $u$ is the
local weak solution of $-(au')'=0$ in the sense of
[[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]. Explicitly
$$u''(x)=-\frac{a'(x)}{a(x)^2}=\begin{cases}-\dfrac1{(2+x)^2},&x<0,\\[2pt] -\dfrac{2}{(2+2x)^2},&x>0,\end{cases}$$
with one-sided limits $-1/4$ at $0^-$ and $-1/2$ at $0^+$; consequently the
one-sided difference quotients of $u'$ at $0$ have the distinct limits
$-1/4$ and $-1/2$, the second classical derivative of $u$ at $0$ does not
exist, and $u\notin C^2(-1,1)$. Thus the weak $H^2$ conclusion of
[[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]] holds for
this Lipschitz coefficient while classical twice differentiability fails:
weak $H^2$ regularity is genuinely weaker than $C^2$.
items.strategy: Compute the primitive explicitly on each side. Its derivative 1/a is Lipschitz, so the piecewise bounded second derivative is the weak derivative and u lies in W^{2,infinity} and H^2. The flux au' is constant, which gives the local weak equation. The unequal one-sided difference quotients of u' show u is not C^2.

items.title: Interior regularity does not imply boundary regularity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Interior smoothness of a weak solution automatically forces $H^2$ up to the
boundary of its domain, so that the interior tangential and normal estimates
suffice at every boundary point.
items.strategy: Use the principal square-root branch on the slit plane. Its imaginary part is smooth and harmonic in the slit disc, lies in H^1 by the polar integral, and is locally weakly harmonic by integration by parts on compact supports. Its radial second derivative has divergent square integral at the slit tip, so it is not H^2 up to the boundary; the domain fails the C^1 graph condition there.

items.title: Boundary $H^2$ regularity needs domain regularity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. In the global $H^2$ Dirichlet theorem the bounded $C^2$ boundary hypothesis
can be replaced by mere Lipschitz regularity: on every bounded Lipschitz
domain in $\mathbb R^2$, every zero-boundary weak solution of
$-\Delta u=f$ with $f\in L^2$ lies in $H^2(\Omega)$.

The reentrant-sector factor $v=r^{\pi/\omega}\sin(\pi\theta/\omega)$ is in
$H^1(S_\omega)\setminus H^2(S_\omega)$ and is locally weakly harmonic.
Multiplying it by a smooth cutoff equal to $1$ near the vertex and $0$ near
the circular boundary gives a zero-boundary weak solution with $L^2$ forcing
that is still not in $H^2$.
items.strategy: Use the reentrant sector harmonic factor v=r^alpha sin(alpha theta), which is in H^1 but not H^2. Multiply by a radial smooth cutoff equal to one near the vertex and supported away from the circular boundary. Cut off near the vertex and in thin angular strips at the radial edges to approximate in H^1 by C_c^∞(S_omega), proving zero trace. The cutoff solution has forcing smooth on an annular sector, hence L^2, but remains non-H^2 near the vertex; the sector is bounded Lipschitz and not C^1.

items.title: The $H^2$ estimate needs the $L^2$ kernel term without injectivity
items.statement:
For every bounded $C^2$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, and every uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator $L$ with bounded coefficients, the estimate
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C\|Lu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$$
holds for every weak solution $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ of the homogeneous Dirichlet problem, with $C$ depending only on the operator and domain data, even when the homogeneous Dirichlet operator has a nontrivial kernel.
items.strategy: On B1 subset R2 take u=1-|x|^2, A(x)=(1/4-|x|^2/8)I, b=0, c=-1. Then A is smooth uniformly elliptic, u is a nonzero H2∩H1_0 function, and -div(A grad u)=u, so Lu=0. Its positive H2 norm cannot be bounded by C||Lu||2; this directly witnesses a kernel in the current n≥2 theorem setting.

items.title: Bootstrapping a smooth Poisson problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (inherited from the embedding theorem used below)
together with Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let
$f\in C^\infty(\Omega)$, and let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak solution
of $-\Delta u=f$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of
[[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]; for instance,
when $\Omega$ is a bounded open set, $u$ may be the zero-trace weak Dirichlet
solution, whose existence and uniqueness under the Axiom of Choice are
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-for-the-weak-dirichlet-poisson-problem]].
Iterating [[thm-interior-h-k-plus-two-elliptic-regularity]] with the
constant coefficients of the Laplacian gives
$u\in H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for every $m$, hence a representative of
class $C^\infty$ by [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], and for that
representative the equation $-\Delta u=f$ holds pointwise on $\Omega$. No
boundary data and no boundary regularity are used: the smoothness of $f$
alone permits the induction to continue at every order.
items.strategy: For each k, apply the higher interior regularity theorem to the Laplacian and smooth datum to obtain every local Sobolev order. In n>=2, apply higher-order embedding to u itself on balls at arbitrarily high orders and patch continuous representatives, which agree everywhere when equal almost everywhere. In n=1, use absolutely continuous representatives of every derivative and the fundamental theorem to identify successive classical derivatives. The a.e. equation becomes pointwise because both sides are continuous.

items.title: Bounded discontinuous elliptic coefficients need not give $H^2$ solutions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Bounded measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients together with $f=0$ force
every $H^1$ weak solution of $-(a^{ij}D_ju)'_i=f$ into $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$,
without any regularity hypothesis on the coefficients.
items.strategy: The piecewise linear u has weak derivative 1 on the left and 1/2 on the right, while au'=1, so integration against compactly supported tests gives the zero weak equation. If u were H^2, its derivative would have an L^1_loc weak derivative; linearity would then give one for the Heaviside class, contradicted by shrinking bumps. Thus bounded measurable ellipticity does not force H^2.

items.title: The reentrant sector singularity has an explicit Sobolev threshold
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\pi<\omega<2\pi$, let $S_\omega=\{(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta):0<r<1,\ 0<\theta<\omega\}$
be the reentrant sector, let $\alpha=\pi/\omega\in(0,1)$, and let
$u(r,\theta)=r^{\alpha}\sin(\alpha\theta)$. Then $\Delta u=0$ in $S_\omega$,
$u$ vanishes on the two radial edges $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\omega$, and for
every integer $m\ge0$
$$u\in H^m(S_\omega)\iff m<1+\alpha=1+\frac{\pi}{\omega};$$
in particular $u\in H^1(S_\omega)\setminus H^2(S_\omega)$ and each additional
whole derivative beyond $H^1$ is unavailable exactly by the deficit
$1-\pi/\omega$. For noninteger $s=m+t$ with integer $m\ge0$ and $0<t<1$, define the intrinsic Slobodeckij scale here by requiring $u\in H^m(S_\omega)$ and finite seminorm $\int_{S_\omega}\int_{S_\omega}\frac{|D^\beta u(x)-D^\beta u(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{2+2t}}\,dx\,dy$ for each weak derivative with $|\beta|=m$. With this convention, for every real $s\ge0$, $u\in H^s(S_\omega)\iff s<1+\alpha=1+\frac{\pi}{\omega}$. The integer threshold follows from polar-coordinate integrals; the fractional threshold follows from a dyadic-shell estimate and a matching scaled-pair lower bound.
items.strategy: For π<ω<2π, take α=π/ω and u=r^α sin(αθ) on the reentrant sector. Polar integration gives the integer Hm threshold m<1+α. For the stated intrinsic Slobodeckij scale, dyadic-shell upper estimates and a matching scaled-pair lower bound give the full real-order threshold s<1+α.

items.title: Higher elliptic regularity cannot gain more than two derivatives
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Even for the constant-coefficient Laplacian in one
dimension, $f\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}$ does not force a weak solution of
$-u''=f$ into $H^{k+3}_{\mathrm{loc}}$: for every integer $k\ge0$ there is
an $H^1$ local weak solution in $H^{k+2}((-1,1))$ whose $(k+3)$rd weak
derivative is not locally square-integrable near an interior point.
items.strategy: For each integer k>=0 set f=|x|^{k+1/2} and u=-A|x|^{k+5/2}, A=((k+5/2)(k+3/2))^{-1}, on (-1,1). Piecewise differentiation shows f in H^k but not H^{k+1} near zero, u in H^{k+2}, and -u''=f distributionally and weakly across zero. If u were H^{k+3} near zero, then f'=-u''' would be H^k there, contradicting f not H^{k+1}.

items.title: Smooth interior data do not repair incompatible Dirichlet corner values
items.statement: On the square $\Omega=(0,1)^2$, every boundary datum whose restriction to each open side is smooth is the boundary trace of a function $u\in C(\overline\Omega)$ harmonic in $\Omega$, that is, satisfying $-\Delta u=0$ there.
items.strategy: For the Laplace Dirichlet problem -Δu=0 on the square, prescribe constant values 1 and 0 on the two adjacent open sides meeting at (0,0), with constant values on the other sides. The unequal side limits contradict continuity at the corner; the H2 extension and embedding argument also rules out a continuous representative of any H2 class realizing those data.
